caption: grandpa broke the same lectern 300 times 📚
logline: A grandpa has broken the same librarian's lectern three hundred times, rerolling her book; ten years ago Grandma rowed to the island across the bay and told him to come back when the sea freezes, and the sea there never freezes, until this morning's book is Frost Walker II.
question: why tf has grandpa broken the same lectern 300 times?
premise: Grandpa has broken the same lectern three hundred times: the librarian holds up a book, he reads it, 'Not THAT one', and breaks the lectern again. His grandkid thinks he just hates that librarian. Grandma lives on the island across the bay; her window is lit every night (the kid: she's scared of the dark). He won't take a boat or build a bridge, ten years (the kid: he's so stubborn). When she left, rowing away, she told him: 'Come back when the sea freezes.' Mom says it never freezes here.
twist: He's been rerolling the librarian for one book, Frost Walker (vanilla: breaking a librarian's lectern before you ever trade with her changes the book she offers; Frost Walker freezes the water under your feet). Grandma's 'when the sea freezes' meant never: Gullwick's bay is cold ocean, which never freezes (only frozen ocean does). He took it literally. This morning the trade screen reads Frost Walker II, Grandpa says nothing, and he walks off the end of the dock as the sea freezes under every step, white ice toward Grandma in her lit window. Her words come true. Cut.

lines.text: My GRANDPA broke / the same LECTERN / three hundred TIMES, / and won't tell me WHY.
lines.say: My grandpa broke the same lectern three hundred times, and won't tell me why.
lines.direction: amazed and fed up, one quick breath; the number lands, then WHY is a real question the kid wants answered
lines.note: STANDARDS 0y: the impossible fact AND the why, by 3 s

lines.text: The LIBRARIAN / holds up a BOOK. / He READS it.
lines.say: The librarian holds up a book. He reads it.
lines.direction: rhythmic, a routine the kid has watched a hundred times; straight into Grandpa

lines.text: And BREAKS it / AGAIN. / I think he just / HATES / that LIBRARIAN.
lines.say: And breaks it again. I think he just hates that librarian.
lines.note: clue 1 (Not THAT one, 300 breaks) and its misreading: a grudge (0a)

lines.text: GRANDMA lives / on that ISLAND. / Her LIGHT'S on / every NIGHT. / I think she's / scared of the DARK.
lines.say: Grandma lives on that island. Her light's on every night. I think she's scared of the dark.
lines.direction: bright, a fact she likes, then a confident little theory
lines.note: someone loved at stake; clue 2 (the light is left on for him) and its misreading: a night light (0a)

lines.text: He WON'T / take a BOAT. / Ten YEARS. / He's SO / STUBBORN.
lines.say: He won't take a boat. Ten years. He's so stubborn.
lines.direction: baffled and a little funny; the last word lands, eye-roll fond
lines.note: clue 3 (no boat: she said the SEA must freeze) and its misreading: stubborn (0a). 'Won't build a bridge' cut for time: the empty water says it

lines.text: When she LEFT, / she TOLD him:
lines.say: When she left, she told him:
lines.direction: leaning in, telling the family legend; straight into her line

lines.text: Come BACK / when the SEA / FREEZES.
lines.say: Come back when the sea freezes.
lines.direction: stubborn, a dare; the last word lands

lines.text: MOM says / it NEVER / freezes HERE.
lines.say: Mom says it never freezes here.
lines.direction: matter-of-fact, a kid repeating what grown-ups say
lines.note: 0a: the kid takes Mom at face value (and she's right: cold ocean never freezes)

lines.text: This MORNING, / the LIBRARIAN / held up / a NEW book.
lines.say: This morning, the librarian held up a new book.
lines.direction: quick, noticing; a lift on NEW; still not suspicious
lines.note: 'the librarian', not 'she' (cold read r6: 'she' read as Grandma). S09 to 'a', S10 (the merchant screen, Frost Walker II) cuts in on NEW: the gamer's clue, never needed by the casual viewer

lines.text: And GRANDPA / DIDN'T break / the LECTERN.
lines.say: And Grandpa didn't break the lectern.
lines.direction: surprised, DIDN'T hit hard; no pause, not scared
lines.note: the rule turned against itself (format beat 5): the lectern stands

lines.text: He put the BOOK / on his BOOTS, / walked OFF / the DOCK, / and the SEA / FROZE / under his FEET.
lines.say: He put the book on his boots, walked off the dock, and the sea froze under his feet.
lines.direction: wide-eyed, plain, each beat a step; the kid says only what they see; FROZE lands with the first ice
lines.note: THE REVEAL, spoken (format beat 6): one plain sentence, no game knowledge; the viewer makes the one jump (the book froze the sea; her words came true)

lines.text: Three hundred LECTERNS. / For a WALK.
lines.say: Three hundred lecterns. For a walk.
lines.direction: a tiny amazed laugh, the kid's understatement; WALK soft
lines.note: the one beat after the reveal; echoes line 1 (three hundred, lecterns) and names the title; cut 1.0 s after WALK
